newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance ministry seeks approval on reform.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance ministry seeks approval on reform.

text.p: A top Thai finance ministry official said on Sunday the ministry was seeking approval for administrative changes to give independence to agencies under its responsibility.

"The finance ministry is now waiting for an approval from the Office of the Civil Service Commission on its request for administrative reform," said Chatumongol Sonakul, permanent secretary for finance.
He said some of the ministry's agencies, for example the Revenue Department, would be working independently like those in developed countries if the approval was given.
Chatumongol was speaking during a seminar on bureaucratic reform organised by the private think-tank, the Thailand Development Research Institute, at the resort of Pattaya.
Some 500 government officials and politicians attended the seminar.
It was organised only two weeks after the new coalition government of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh came into power following a general election on November 17.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan is due to announce his fiscal and monetary programmes on Tuesday as part of a government confidence-building programme.
